Mirana cannot Leap when rooted/leashed.
Undying's Tombstone zombies can be annoying for Mirana to deal with since they tank Sacred Arrow.

tips.text: Boundless Strike's damage is applied as an instant attack . This instant attack ignores disarms, has true strike, and applies attack modifiers (except cleave). If you have an attack modifier with a proc, it'll roll for a chance to proc on each target hit.
notes: Since Boundless Strike is an instant attack, it'll break your Smoke if it damages a unit.

tips.text: If you Boundless Strike Mud Golems to death, the Shard Golems will also get hit by the Boundless Strike as they spawn. Small farming efficiency note.

No matter how many targets are hit in Boundless Strike, only one Jingu Mastery stack is consumed. If you're low on HP and have Jingu active, try saving Boundless to smack an entire creep wave and lifesteal off every target.

You can't place Jingu stacks on illusions. An optimist sees this as a way to identify the real Phantom Lancer with a Boundless Strike, a pessimist would be angry they can't tap that unattended Terrorblade illusion for a free Jingu.
If you save your first skill point in Tree Dance, you can skill it up and immediately cast it after taking damage since the damage cooldown is only in effect after the spell is learned.

You can keep an Iron Branch in your pocket to create a tree to Dance off of on demand. Usually this is pointless given the density of trees around the map, but if you're mid you could take someone by surprise by Primal Springing on them straight from the river.
You're considered two 'levels' of high ground elevation up when perched during Tree Dance, but enemy units will have vision of you at their ground level whenever you're jumping from tree to tree.
Ground targeted spells will still affect you as normal when you're on a tree.
Casting Boundless Strike or Mischief won't unperch you from a tree, but finishing a Wukong's Command cast will. You can use items, like TP, without getting unperched.
The enemy will hear your Primal Spring channeling sound at wherever the landing is targeted.
You can Tree Dance through a Disruptor's Kinetic Field, but you cannot Primal Spring through it.

If Mars casts an Arena within ~3000 range of your hero, you just straight up will not be allowed to cast Tree Dance on anything. You can attempt to cast Primal Spring if you're already on a tree, but if the Arena is still up when the channel ends, you'll just walk off your tree and put the spell on cooldown.

Agh's Shard Boundless Strike applies a lower strength Primal Spring debuff on enemies. However, if you've already applied a stronger Primal Spring debuff onto a target, hitting them with Agh's Shard Boundless Strike will refresh that stronger debuff.
Here are a few Mischief interactions:
notes: When in Mischief, you won't appear on the enemy minimap at all. Handy for courier sniping or sneaking through warded areas.
Enemy towers and creeps won't attack you when you're in Mischief.

The first 0.1s of Mischief provides damage immunity from any source. It's not a disjoint and it's not a banish, but you can prevent taking damage from any incoming projectiles/attacks/damage over time ticks for that period.
You can instantly drop aggro from creeps by going into Mischief.
Right clicking heroes while in Mischief won't draw aggro from creeps, but creeps will aggro you as soon as you start your attack.
Activating Mischief in most situations will turn you into a Courier, Iron Branch, Clarity, Salve, TP Scroll, Tango, or a banana.
If you're standing next to a non-hero unit, like a lane/neutral creep or summoned unit (excluding creep-heroes), you'll turn into that unit.

Other transformations are location dependent. Standing near a tree will make you a tree. Rosh pit will make you an Aegis, Cheese, Refresher Shard, or Roshan himself. Rune spot will make you a bounty or power rune depending on location.
The enemy can't see the Jingu Mastery buff over your head when you're in Mischief, but debuffs (like Dust or Ursa's Fury Swipes) will still show above your disguise.
You can instantly lose a Troll Warlord's Battle Trance aggro by going into Mischief. This is more consistent to pull off if there are other aggro targets available for him to shift focus onto.

tips.text: Wukong's Command soldiers can't proc Basher/Abyssal or Echo Sabre, but they can proc every other on-hit item effect. They also individually carry whatever auras your hero has.
notes: Wukong soldiers do not copy your neutral item.

tips.text: Agh's Scepter soldiers won't attack buildings unless the real Monkey King is within 500 range of them.
Agh's Scepter soldiers will disappear when you die, even if you have an Aegis.
When using Changing of the Guard, enemies won't be able to see the ring surrounding the soldier you transformed to, only allies can.
You disjoint incoming projectiles and are invulnerable while in Changing of the Guard.

counters.text: Tree Dance follows a stricter set of Blink Dagger rules in terms of going on cooldown when damaged, so damage over time debuffs, like from like Urn, help make Monkey King a little less slippery. It's stricter than Blink Dagger because even damage from lane/neutral creeps will put it on cooldown.

Destroying the tree Monkey King is perched on will stun him for a hefty period of time. Not many heroes can easily take advantage of this, but: Beastmaster's Wild Axes, Windranger's Powershot, Storm Spirit's Ball Lightning, Phoenix's Icarus Dive and Supernova, Enigma's Midnight Pulse, Keeper of the Light's Agh's Scepter Will-O-Wisp, Mars's Arena of Blood, Underlord's Fiend's Gate, Timbersaw's everything, Earth Spirit's everything, Batrider's Firefly, or Kez's Echo Slash are a few examples of spells that are either fast enough or large enough to catch a Tree Dancing Monkey King by surprise.
notes: Don't forget about the tree cutting capabilities of Quelling Blade or Battle Fury late game.

Roshan's Banner is a long range instant cast item that destroys trees in a fairly large AoE. In a late game situation, it could be worth sitting on the Banner in your inventory to stun a Tree Dancing Monkey King.
Force Staffed units can destroy trees.
Harpoon can target trees and will destroy all trees in your travel path.

counters.text: You'll need vision of him to even know what tree he's on to begin with. Heroes with vision providing spells like Razor's Plasma Field, Disruptor's Thunder Strike, Puck's Illusory Orb, Drow Ranger's Agh's Shard Glacier, or Nature's Prophet's Agh's Shard Curse of the Oldgrowth can be handy.
notes: For items that provide vision, Essence Distiller can be ground targeted and provide vision in its AoE and Shiva's Guard's active also provides a lot of flying vision.

counters.text: Monkey's Jingu Mastery damage+lifesteal buff can be removed with basic dispels. This makes heroes like Oracle with Fortune's End or Enchantress with Enchant useful in the laning phase or Shadow Demon with Demonic Purge useful in the late game.
notes: However, be aware that Monkey King has a "Jingu Mastery Undispellable" talent.

counters.text: The audio cue from Primal Spring is played based on your camera placement. For example, if you hear the guzheng to your left, he targeted the Spring on the left side of whatever your camera's looking at.
Wukong's Command soldiers' right clicks can be reduced by damage block from Vanguard or Crimson Guard.

You can try shoving Monkey King out of his Wukong's Command circle to end the spell with a Force Staff if he's near the edge or use spells that Fear or spells that apply forced movement or knockback like Batrider's Flamebreak or Keeper of the Light's Blinding Light.

Glyphing the creep wave can be an effective way to minimize the amount of lifesteal MK gets from a Boundless Strike if he has Jingu ready. This is mainly relevant when you're laning against him. Just be sure you have a hotkey assigned to your Glyph to pull this trick off quickly.

tips.text: Try hugging trees whenever it's convenient to take advantage of the damage given from your Spirit of the Forest innate.
notes: Treants also benefit from the Spirit of the Forest innate damage.

tips.text: Sprout gives a small radius of flying vision around the trees when cast. Use Sprout to scout enemies who are juking in fog, counter ward cliffs, or to get that last hit on the flying courier who just flew out of vision.

Target your Sprout during the Teleport animation when you're going in for a gank. You'll cast it as soon as you're in range and have vision of the target rather than fumbling around the moment you get there.
Sprout can be hero targeted. However, you can utilize ground targeting if the enemy has a Linken's Sphere or if you're trying to guess where an invis hero went.
notes: It can also be worthwhile to ground target the entire Sprout ahead of the enemy in a chokepoint. Most enemies will have ways to cut through a single tree, but not many can quickly cut their way through multiple trees.

tips.text: If you ground target Sprout from fog, you won't reveal yourself to the enemy who gets hit by it. If you directly target them, they'll get vision of you.
notes: This is true for any spell that has the option between ground and direct unit targeting. If you ever directly target an enemy unit, the enemy team will briefly get vision of your hero. If you ground target, you won't be revealed through fog.

tips.text: You can Sprout enemy towers to block their vision. This is really only useful if you need to briefly reduce enemy vision around a tower for some reason, like during a dive. Remember that attacking any unit gives that team vision of the attacking unit, so you can't attack a tower without it seeing you.
notes: You can also Sprout your team's buildings defensively. However, your towers will still shoot at enemies if you have vision of them, which in turn gives enemies vision of your attacking tower. Defensive Sprouting is mainly useful on buildings that don't attack, like your barracks or your Ancient.

That's right, your Ancient. The big ass building you're trying to protect apparently cannot be seen by enemies if you Sprout the middle of it. This interaction could buy you some valuable seconds in a final defense. Defense of the Ancient.

tips.text: Casting Sprout on a target in Clockwerk's Power Cogs will always shove everyone except the main target out of the Cogs.
Always carry a TP scroll. A scroll gives you an immediate escape after you finish Teleporting in to snipe a courier, kill a fleeing hero, or cut the creep wave.
Courier sniping is relevant all game long. Consider buying your own observer wards and planting them in areas that can spot couriers traveling to and from the fountain or secret shop.
95% of the raising the roof animation for Teleport will stay under the invis granted by Shadow Blade or an invis rune.
You can use press the 'Cancel Current Action'/stop hotkey at any point of the Teleportation cast animation to cancel it without putting it on cooldown.
notes: You can use Teleportation to mindgame enemies. If you see your teammate is getting ganked, start casting a Teleport right on top of the enemies, even if you only have 10 HP, just to freak them out. The animation is pretty obvious and is long enough that you can easily cancel it.

tips.text: When ganking in the early game, Teleport into places out of vision like inside trees or behind the lane.
Memorize the timings of important objectives around the map, like runes and Shrines of Wisdom, so you can Teleport and steal them from the enemy.
You can teleport into the treelines around the enemy base to safely/sneakily plant high ground wards behind enemy barracks before a siege.
How to avoid dying as Prophet:
notes: Step 1: Run away a little bit.
Step 2: Cast Sprout on yourself (if you have the "Double Tap Ability to Self Cast" setting enabled, just double tap the hotkey) so no one can see you during your private time.
Step 3: Double tap the Teleport hotkey to automatically target the fountain.
Step 4: Do it all over again in a minute because the enemy never learns.

tips.text: Treants are great units for distracting a creep wave. Just send one up ahead to lead the enemy creeps on a wild goose chase while you continue beating on the tower.
Treants are great units for scouting. Send them on choke points where you don't have vision to keep track of enemy whereabouts.
Treants are great units for blocking camps. They move fast and are usually too tanky for enemies to kill if you plop them down right before a camp is about to spawn.
Treants have free pathing through trees on the map.

Learn how Wrath of Nature works and how to maximize the damage on high priority targets. It has the same number of bounces at all levels, so you typically want to cast it if you can see heroes on the minimap and at least 2 lanes have creeps fighting at the moment.
Linken's Sphere will pop if you directly target Wrath of Nature onto an enemy hero, but the spell will continue bouncing. You can use this to globally pop an enemy Linken's Sphere on demand.
Agh's Scepter Wrath of Nature is a "bind" which roots and disarms targets for the debuff duration.

counters.text: QUELLING BLAAAAADE. Also Tangoes or Battle Fury. Few spells can lose effectiveness so dramatically as Sprout does from such cheap items. If your ally is Sprouted, be a pal and use one of these to get them out.
notes: Learn which spells can break trees as well (especially the not so obvious ones like Io's Tether, Leshrac's Split Earth, Lina's Light Strike Array, Undying's Tombstone, Kez's Echo Slash, etc). These can also come in handy to destroy NP's little circle. Keep at least 1 Tango or QB item on hand in the mid game if you don't have any of these spells and late game.

counters.text: Force Staff can destroy trees, such as from Sprout.
Harpoon can target trees and will destroy all trees in your travel path. Handy solution for melee carries to get out of Sprout.
The barrier NP gets after Teleportation can be removed with dispels.
Keep a close eye on your courier. You can protect it with the Shield or Speed Burst if Prophet is trying to make a move on it.

If you see Wrath of Nature bouncing around, back out of the lane to get out of vision and stay there for a few seconds. If you're wondering how his ult just hit you in the middle of your jungle, you may be under an enemy ward.

Save your stun/silence for the end of his Teleport animation. He's effectively disabling himself for free while he's standing still mid-animation. Let him think that he's going to get out while you're whittling him down with auto attacks, then disable his cast at the last moment.
Prophet faces in the direction that he's Teleporting. While not always useful, if you see him Teleporting you can warn your teammates where he's probably traveling to.
Nature's Prophet can't cast Teleportation while rooted/leashed.

tips.text: You get innate Sadist regen stacks off of any unit you kill including buildings, wards, and creep denies. The only exceptions are illusions or Arc Warden's Tempest Double.

"Nah they're dead, Death Pulse will get them." No. Death Pulse never gets them. Somehow enemies will inevitably heal just barely enough HP in time and you'll be left wondering, "Wait, they didn't die?" Always finish the kill either with Heartstopper Aura, Reaper's Scythe, or auto attacks.
Death Pulse can hit invis and fogged units.
Heartstopper Aura will deal damage to enemies in fog, but they won't see a Heartstopper debuff in their status bar if they don't have vision of you.
notes: You can't cheat this to see if enemies have vision of you or not, however. Your team will always see the Heartstopper debuff in an enemy's status bar regardless of if they have vision of you or not.

tips.text: Ghost Shroud boosts HP/mana regen given to you from all sources, including teammates. Shroud yourself before a Keeper of the Light Chakra Magic or Omniknight Purification or Mekansm/Greaves or Arcane Boots.
notes: Also, Ghost Shroud yourself before using a Magic Wand or Healing Lotus for the regen amp.

tips.text: Ghost Shroud's ethereal state makes you immune to physical damage even from spells, such as Juggernaut's Omnislash or Bristleback's Quill Spray.

Ghost Shroud's ethereal state does not work if you are debuff immune/BKB'd because debuff immunity removes your ethereal state. This is true for any hero if they activate Ghost Scepter or Ethereal Blade during BKB.
You get permanent Reaper's Scythe stacks off Aegis kills or Wraith King Reincarnation kills.
Agh's Shard Death Seeker can be a useful spell to break Linken's Sphere so you can Reaper's Scythe a target.

Mechanically, Agh's Shard Death Seeker hides/banishes your hero at the casting location and then moves you to the targeted location once the projectile lands. You're basically Puck Phase Shifted while the Death Seeker projectile is flying.
notes: The ending location is determined on cast. Even if the enemy Force Staff's themselves after being targeted by Death Seeker, you'll still appear where they were when you cast the spell.

You remain hidden/untargetable and invulnerable throughout the movement. The invulnerability is relevant because if you're Ruptured by Bloodseeker, you can Death Seeker somewhere without taking any damage. The hide is relevant because spells that go through invulnerability, like Silencer's Global Silence, won't be able to debuff you since you're hidden.
You can use Death Seeker to avoid spells like Disruptor's Glimpse and Kunkka's X Marks, or go through Disruptor's Kinetic Field and Mars's Arena.

counters.text: You can't disjoint Death Pulse, so don't bother trying.
Pipe or Glimmer Cape's magic damage barrier can potentially save an ally's life against Reaper's Scythe.

Dazzle's Shallow Grave, Oracle's Fate's Edict and False Promise, and heroes that can banish a Scythed target like Shadow Demon, Outworld Destroyer, and Tusk are also good counters. A well-timed Bane Nightmare provides momentary invulnerability as well.
You can potentially use Wind Waker on an ally being Scythed to save them.
Ghost Shroud can be dispelled off Necrophos the same ways as Ghost Scepter can be (spells like Enchantress's Enchant, Largo's Catchy Lick, Oracle's Fortune's End, Shadow Demon's Demonic Purge, etc).
notes: If you're a carry and you're struggling to right click Necro because of Ghost Shroud, you can get a Nullifier or Disperser to dispel the ethereal state off.

counters.text: Necro is taking bonus magic damage whenever he's in Ghost Shroud, so try to bait it out before tossing high magic damage nukes.
The HP Necrophos heals can be reduced by debuffs that affect health restoration:
notes: Items that can reduce health restoration: Spirit Vessel, Orb of Frost/Corrosion, Eye of Skadi, Crella's Crozier, as well as the "Crippling Crossbow" and "Jidi Pollen Bag" neutral item artifacts.

Spells that can reduce health restoration: Abaddon's Withering Mist innate, Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast, Doom's Doom, Drow Ranger's Agh's Scepter Hypothermia, Pudge's Agh's Scepter Rot, Slark's Saltwater Shiv, and a few others.

counters.text: Necro loves playing against heroes who frequently give Stick charges, especially in lane. Try casting spells from fog since Magic Stick only gives charges if the spell caster is in vision.
Necro can't cast Agh's Shard Death Seeker while rooted/leashed.

tips.text: Nyx gets the luxury of easy positioning thanks to Vendetta to make multi hero Impales simpler. Vendetta one hero and then roughly target the Impale on another hero. Since you're in such close range to your first target, you will most likely nyx them both with the Impale.

You can stack certain neutral camps with Impale. This only works on some camps, however. The reason is because Impale raises the creeps above the spawn box check height, but different camps have different heights. You'll have to test it in a lobby yourself (use the -spawnneutrals command with cheats enabled) to see which camps work and which ones don't. The timing is extremely close, you have to nyx the spell at ~59s.

If you see an enemy with a Lotus Orb on, you can activate Spiked Carapace and then cast Mind Flare on them. They'll reflect the Mind Flare and then instantly get stunned by the Carapace because they damaged you. Remote nyxing.
Spiked Carapace blocks an entire damage instance, so Blink Dagger and regen won't be broken if the Carapace reflects the damage source. Nyx.
notes: If you're playing against a Bloodseeker and you get Ruptured when you have Blink Dagger, you can activate Spiked Carapace and Blink so the entire ~1200 range Rupture damage instance nyxes onto BS.

tips.text: Spiked Carapace will instantly come out after banishes and nyx enemies from damage sources like Eul's cyclone or Outworld Destroyer's Astral Imprisonment.

You can cast Spiked Carapace while in Vendetta and the invis won't be removed. Try to Nyx yourself into enemy AoE spells while in Vendetta to get an easy setup for your combo. This is especially useful when playing against enemies who finish off creep waves with spells like Lina with Dragon Slave or Puck with Illusory Orb.

Other less obvious sources of damage can also be handy to Carapace yournyx into, like heroes with cleave or Radiance, Ember Spirit's Immolation innate, Batrider's Firefly trail, or even Templar Assassin's Psi Blades since they hit invisible units.
notes: Spells that use ward units to deal damage will not interact with Carapace. For example, Witch Doctor's Death Ward is considered an independent damage source, so nyxing into a Death Ward with Carapace on will not stun or damage Witch Doctor.

tips.text: Vendetta's damage is great in the early/mid game, but you're better off using the invisibility to get good Impale positioning in the late game. Enemies will have BKBs and be grouped up late game, making it a lot harder to fully nyx someone without them reacting. Don't get greedy with Vendetta attacks if you don't need the damage, just go straight for the Impale while you're invisible.
You can nyx yourself into Vendetta while you're channeling a TP (like all other invis spells).
Be on the map as little as possible. The less time you spend nyxing around in lane, the less willing the enemies are to farm if they don't know where you are.
Vendetta is a great spell to eighty-nyx couriers with. Try setting up observer wards to catch courier paths so you can snipe them.
While in Agh's Scepter Burrow, you can use items like Force Staff or Harpoon to move your nyx around. You can't use Blink Dagger or TP, however, because you're considered rooted while Burrowed.

counters.text: Be aware of your damage sources. Nyx can Carapace stun you off of things like Radiance burn or any damage over time source you put on him. You can toggle Radiance while TPing.
Be wary of using Lotus Orbs when against Nyx. He can target you with Mind Flare and have Carapace pre-casted to stun you when you least expect it.

Resist the urge to retaliate whenever he blows his full combo on you. Nyxes almost always Carapace as soon as they finish their sequence. Just walk away. Be the bigger person. Don't stun/kill yourself.
Try to bait out Nyx's Carapace by casting and canceling spells with long and obvious animations or even canceling attack animations.
Keep your eyes on the scoreboard in the first 10 minutes of the game to see when Nyx hits level 6. Most Nyxes will leave the map as soon as they have access to Vendetta, so get some sentries ready.
Essence Distiller can provide true sight on the debuffed target, such as Nyx in Vendetta.
The Vendetta break debuff can be removed with basic dispels.
Nyx's Agh's Scepter Burrow mound still "faces" a direction, so you can potentially use an offensive Force Staff to shove him further into your team.

tips.text: Swashbuckle sets your damage flat and attacks every unit in the AoE multiple times. There are a few interactions to note:
notes: Even though there are several... swashes? Each target receives their own individual 'attack' per swash strike. A Javelin Piercing one target doesn't mean every target will get Pierced on the same strike.
Each attack will burn mana with Diffusal Blade.
Crits are not great because they multiply off of Swashbuckle's damage, not your attack damage.
Basher gives you a pretty high probability of Bashing a target in Swashbuckle, but only one unit in the AoE can ever get bashed due to Basher's cooldown.
Maelstrom also has a cooldown, but you can potentially proc it twice in a Swashbuckle.
Quelling Blade doesn't add damage to creeps in Swashbuckle.
Cleave can take advantage of the individual Swashbuckle attacks since each target will proc its own cleave AoE.

If you slide through a target while traveling in Swashbuckle, you have an instance of Swashbuckle damage around your hero. The collision size for this damage instance is tiny, but it gives you another chance to proc a Lucky Shot or item effect.
Swashbuckle attacks can kill Undying Tombstone zombies.

tips.text: Swashbuckle attacks have true strike and work through disarms.
Since Swashbuckle counts as an instant attack , it'll break your Smoke if it damages a unit.

Swashbuckle and Shield Crash's movements are classed as forced movement. You can use them to move up and down cliffs, travel through trees without destroying them, and break out of spells like Disruptor's Kinetic Field.

You don't always have to Swashbuckle backwards, you know? Sometimes if you're escaping and there's no chance of landing a Swashbuckle hit on a pursuing enemy, you may just be giving away your position by sending Swashbuckle attacks into their vision.
Every time you successfully hit a hero in Shield Crash, the barrier amount increments and the buff is refreshed.
Your Shield Crash barrier incrementing could be a way to verify if enemies are hiding nearby in fog or invisible.
Shield Crash's barrier buff doesn't factor illusions as valid heroes, but it does factor clones. Like Meepo. Sweet, sweet Meepo.

Because barriers, like from Shield Crash, prevent your actual HP from being touched, you can use regen like Bottle without it getting broken as long as the barrier is taking the damage. This also prevents your Blink Dagger from getting broken when taking enemy damage.

You're disabled during the Shield Crash animation when walking, but you're not disabled during the Shield Crash animation when Rolling. This means that you can cancel a Rolling Shield Crash into Swashbuckle to move your Shield Crash landing AoE.

Each Agh's Scepter Swashbuckle AoE from Shield Crash slightly overlaps in the corners around your hero. You can potentially deal more damage to a target if you Shield Crash next to them diagonally to hit them with both the horizontal and vertical Swashbuckle swipes.

If you shift+queue Blink Dagger+Shield Crash during your Rolling Thunder cast animation, you'll blink to the location and Shield Crash vertically in place. However, your Rolling Thunder will not damage or stun enemies until after the Shield Crash cast finishes landing.
If you cancel Rolling Thunder in the middle of jumping in Shield Crash, you'll immediately drop down and Shield Crash in place without keeping the Rolling Thunder momentum.
You can jump off the edges of the map in Rolling Thunder with Shield Crash. I can really only see this being useful if you want to hide yourself as you TP out if you think the enemy can cancel it.
When playing against Rubick, immediately Shield Crash after going into Rolling Thunder. Putting Shield Crash on cooldown is usually worth preventing Rubick from Spell Stealing your ult.
All items work while in Rolling Thunder:
notes: You can channel a TP while Rolling.
You can Blink while Rolling. You'll continue Rolling in the same direction after Blinking.
You can Eul's yourself while Rolling to multihit a single enemy without needing to bounce.
If you don't press anything except for the Shield Crash hotkey while in the Eul's cyclone, you'll do stationary Shield Crash in-place after landing.
You can Harpoon an enemy while Rolling to drag yourself towards them for a stun.

tips.text: In general, if you have to "path" around an object on the map, you can probably bounce into it during Rolling Thunder. Here are some notes:
notes: Most buildings on the map don't count. You can't bounce into towers, barracks, the ancient, Outposts, Twin Gates, or Shrines of Wisdom.
You can bounce into the Lotus Pool, surprisingly.
You can usually bounce into the random map features like Radiant crystals and stuff sticking out of the ground.
The secret shop owners can be bounced into. The Radiant secret shop owner has a pretty janky hitbox, though.
You can bounce into Clockwerk's Power Cogs, Earthshaker's Fissure, Tusk's Ice Shards, and Drow Ranger's Agh's Shard Glacier.

tips.text: You can mess with Rolling Thunder's trajectory by repeatedly attempting to enter a Twin Gate or an Underlord's Fiend's Gate.

You can drive by an Outpost or Watcher and channel it in the middle of Rolling Thunder. Just make sure you're fine with traveling in a straight line for a few seconds because changing your direction will cancel the channel.
It's impossible to perma-chain stun an enemy with Rolling Thunder. Even with perfect bounces, they can always get a BKB or instant cast spell off between bumps.
Rolling Thunder provides debuff immunity and also serves as a basic dispel on cast.
Agh's Shard Roll Up provides debuff immunity but does not apply a dispel on your hero.

Normally, roots/leashes prevent you from using your movement spells. However, you can cast Agh's Shard Roll Up through roots/leashes. If the disable does not pierce debuff immunity, then you should be able to Rolling Thunder or Swashbuckle while in Roll Up.
Hitting someone in Chronosphere with Rolling Thunder will damage and bump them away like normal and you'll continue Rolling in place on the edge of the Chrono.

The moment you ricochet off a wall, there's an extremely small window of time when you can click in the same direction you were traveling to keep bumping into the same wall. It requires nearly tick perfect timing, but there's no harm in going for it.
notes: If you're committed to using this trick, there is a method to consistently pull this off and perma-bounce against a wall. If you have a mouse with a freescrolling wheel, type in your console: bind mwheeldown mc_move And enable the "Quick Move" setting in the settings menu. This will bind the move command to your mousewheel down and makes your hero act whenever a move hotkey is pressed. Now you can spin mousewheel down to issue a million move commands at once which solves the whole 'timing' issue with this trick.
"But Tsunami, the 'Auto-repeat Right Mouse' setting already exists!" Yup and even that doesn't click fast enough to pull this tech off.

tips.text: Pangolier is the only hero in the game that doesn't have to turn to cast items.
Lucky Shot's debuff works on Rosh.

counters.text: Pangolier can't cast Swashbuckle or Rolling Thunder if he's rooted/leashed.
The Shield Crash barrier can be dispelled off Pango.
Leashes/roots that go through debuff immunity (like Grimstroke's Soulbind) will cause Pango's Rolling Thunder do a burnout and just spin in place.
Stuns that go through debuff immunity won't cancel Rolling Thunder, but Pango will stop moving during the stun.
notes: The only exception is Primal Beast's Pulverize. For some reason Pulverize instantly cancels Rolling Thunder.

counters.text: Bloodseeker's Rupture forces Pangolier to make some tough choices about life while Rolling.
Pango is only debuff immune in Rolling Thunder. He can still be attacked and take damage. Difficult if you're a melee hero, but ranged heroes can still hit him easily.

If you're touching a high/low ground cliff, Pango may push you to the other level of terrain with the Rolling Thunder bump. Try hugging a cliff if he's about to run you over to possibly escape the pinball machine.

The occasional question marks you see pop up above Pango sometimes when attacking him are from his Fortune Favors the Bold innate. This innate makes it so enemy attack modifiers with proc chances randomly may not work on Pango. For example, if you roll a Faceless Void Time Lock proc, it may just not bash him.
notes: The Fortune Favors the Bold innate can be disabled by breaks.

Breaks can be provided with items like Silver Edge or Khanda. Spells that Break include Doom's Agh's Scepter Doom, Hoodwink's Sharpshooter, Naga Siren's Agh's Scepter Ensnare, Nyx Assassin's Vendetta, Phantom Assassin's Agh's Scepter Fan of Knives, Shadow Demon's Agh's Scepter Demonic Purge, Viper's Viper Strike, and a few others.

tips.text: Doppelganger allows you to travel up and down cliffs.
Doppelganger breaks trees upon landing. Use this to find juking enemies or to create quicker jungle routes.
The brighter of the two illusions from Doppelganger is the one that takes 100% damage. You can assign this one to a control group and it will stick each time Doppelganger is used.
notes: Much like every other illusion hero out there, you can sometimes be tricky by microing an illusion out of the pack to bait enemies into thinking it's the real you. The ruse is even more convincing with this 100% damage received illusion.

tips.text: Doppelganger can dispel all the debuffs that a Manta Style would... except for roots and silences because you literally can't cast the spell when rooted or silenced.
Casting Doppelganger adds 2 seconds duration to any gathered illusions.
Treat Doppelganger's banish like Puck's Phase Shift when playing against a team with a lot of projectile spells.

If you get jumped by an enemy and need to banish yourself quickly, cast Doppelganger in the same direction your hero is facing rather than turning around. PL's turn rate is average, but every millisecond can count when escaping.

Doppelganger forces your hero's location to the target area once the banish ends. This allows you to outplay spells like Disruptor's Glimpse or Kunkka's X Marks the Spot which typically take repositioning priority.

When Roshing, you can click on Rosh to see the cooldown on his Slam. Rosh will always cast it once his attack animation ends and it's off cooldown. Doppelganger during the cast animation to avoid you and your illusions taking a bunch of unnecessary damage.
Phantom Rush can be toggled on or off. This is useful in the laning phase if you only want it to trigger when last hitting specific creeps.
If you see a unit across a cliff, but you're in Phantom Rush range, PL will sprint to it taking the quickest pathing possible.
Phantom Rush is always toggled on for Juxtapose illusions and will always be off cooldown when they spawn.
Don't forget to utilize Phantom Rush when escaping. Sprint to a neutral or enemy lane creep to get the speed boost. Phantom Rush will even work on enemy buildings and ward units.
Phantom Rush speed overrides any slowing debuffs that your hero or illusions are under.
When tower diving, attack+move/force attack (default a+left click) your illusions during attack backswings to attempt to shake tower aggro momentarily.
notes: Use attack+move/force attack when taking jungle camps or Rosh to relieve yourself of creep aggro once you generate some illusions.

tips.text: You can use the "Next Unit" hotkey in your settings to rapid fire cycle through your illusions and send them in a bunch of different directions to cause chaos when you're escaping an enemy.

Juxtapose doesn't multiply on buildings, but does on wards. This makes PL very effective against things like Shadow Shaman's Mass Serpent Wards, Pugna's Nether Ward, Undying's Tombstone, Venomancer's Plague Wards, and Zeus's Nimbus.
notes: Illusions don't deal damage to Phoenix's Supernova, but you can Juxtapose off hitting it.

counters.text: Try to bait out Doppelganger by animation canceling spells.

If you think you've finally found the real PL and started targeting a spell on him, resist the urge to keep mashing the hotkey. You may inadvertently cancel the cast and lose him again in the Sea of Lancers.

Some debuffs that can help identify the real PL that can't be dispelled by Doppelganger: Bloodseeker's Rupture, Huskar's Burning Spears, Invoker's Deafening Blast, Shadow Demon's Shadow Poison, Ursa's Fury Swipes, Viper's Viper Strike, Windranger's Focus Fire, Witch Doctor's Maledict, and Nullifier's active.
notes: Monkey King's Jingu Mastery counter can't be dispelled and the counter doesn't apply on illusions. So if you Boundless Strike his army, you'll immediately be able to find the real PL.
Dazzle's Nothl Projection Poison Touch hexing and Skywrath Mage's Mystic Flare are examples of AoE spells that instantly kill illusions.
Brewmaster's Storm Brewling Dispel Magic does substantial damage to illusions.

counters.text: Another useful method to identifying the real PL is to quickly check his Magic Wand charges. PL illusions will duplicate the number of charges the real hero has when they're created, but won't get new charges unlike the real PL. This is mainly useful when he's escaping with Doppelganger and trying to juke you with his tanky illusion.

Rubick can't Spell Steal from illusions. You can mash Spell Steal on PL's army to vaguely identify the real one since all the fake illusions will give Spell Steal an error. The error works even when Spell Steal is out of range, so you can globally identify the real PL with this.
Skywrath Mage's Concussive Shot will never select illusions to hit first, it'll always try to find a real hero in the AoE.
While Morphling can't copy PL's Juxtapose as a Morph, Spirit Lance/Doppelganger illusions created by a Morphed PL can Juxtapose, allowing you to create your own PL army by proxy.
Phantom Lancer can't cast Doppelganger while rooted/leashed.
Mjollnir's Static Shield active has a chance to proc off of every PL illusion whacking you.
Crimson Guard's active basically neutralizes all illusion damage.
Phantom Lancer and his illusions heavily lean on physical damage, so build armor.

tips.text: When using Battery Assault in lane, position yourself so that the enemy creeps won't absorb hits. Stand along the outer perimeter of an enemy hero, rather than bulldozing through the middle of the creep wave.
Avoid immediately right clicking the enemy hero and drawing creep aggro when you're going in with Battery Assault in lane.

Battery Assault can't hit invis or untargetable units, but Power Cogs can. So if an enemy Templar Assassin uses Meld or a Slark goes into Shadow Dance, be aware that the shock on Cogs can still hit them.
When you walk on top of your Power Cogs, they briefly retract into the ground. While retracted, the Cogs won't block pathing for allies and won't shock enemies.
If Clockwerk attempts to deny a Power Cog, you'll attack it and it'll slide it straight ahead of your hero.
The shock on Power Cogs counts as a stun. Even if Battery Assault is on cooldown, you can still cancel enemy TPs if you hit them with Cogs.
notes: Setting up Cogs right beside an Aegis grave can give you an instant disable when an enemy respawns.
Power Cogs won't shock enemies inside the Cog circle even if you hit a Cog at them. It can only shock enemies outside the circle.

tips.text: Power Cogs will freeze when hit into the edge of a Faceless Void's Chronosphere. However, once a Cog is already affected by Chrono, Clock can hit it again and it'll fly through the Chrono.
Using Cogs as an area denial tool is just as useful as locking someone in. Use it to prevent enemies from chasing you or use it during high ground tower defenses.
If you're offlaning, consider using Cogs to lock your lane creeps in at the beginning of the game so the waves meet closer to your tower.
Power Cogs destroy all trees within the circle and pushed Cogs also destroy trees in their path.

Consider planting Cogs near your team during high ground sieges to preempt an enemy who's trying to Blink in and initiate on your team. If they do, they may immediately get shocked when they Blink in.

Power Cogs give a small radius of vision. Consider punching a few into enemy high grounds or other fogged areas to scout. You can also try dewarding by spawning a Power Cog on a cliff for vision instead of wasting your Rocket Flare cooldown.

Rocket Flares give vision on detonation, we all know that, but the vision provided during the Flare's flight is just as important. Make a decision whether you want vision of a small area for a long time or a large area for a short time. If you are policing the Rosh pit, detonate the Flare there. If you're trying to get information about where the enemies are during a lull, let it fly all over their jungle and explode somewhere useless. Ideally, you can do both in one Flare and get a double kill where it explodes, but that's not always going to happen.
In late game situations, consider using Rocket Flare vision to keep track of power runes.
If you are within ~1800 range of a neutral camp, you can draw aggro and stack it with Rocket Flare.
A target can get hit by two Agh's Scepter Overclocked Rocket Flares if you target the primary Flare ~200 units or more left/right off center.
You can Hookshot to allied units, neutrals, Tormentor, or Rosh. Keep this in mind if Hook is off cooldown and you're getting ganked.
Hookshot stuns debuff immune/BKB'd enemies.

Clockwerk will briefly stun everything in his path while flying to a Hookshotted target. Normally this isn't relevant since the only target you'll usually collide with is the one you landed the Hook on. However, if you quickly change your 'starting' location after casting Hookshot with something like Blink Dagger, you can change your trajectory and use your flying body as a debuff immune piercing disable.
Cancel the cast animation for Hookshot with your 'Cancel Current Action'/stop hotkey to bait enemies into juking for no reason.
You can interrupt Hookshot from dragging Clockwerk to his target by self-casting Force Staff or Eul's mid-flight.
You can toggle Agh's Shard Jetpack on and off.
You can cast items while flying in Agh's Shard Jetpack. In fact, you don't even have to turn your hero to target items (or spells) if you cast them mid-Jetpack. You can even TP while Jetpacking.

You can channel an Outpost or Watcher while Jetpacking. Just be sure you're happy with the direction you're traveling before you start because you'll have to keep moving in a straight line until the channel completes.
notes: If you channel a Twin Gate or Underlord Fiend's Gate while Jetpacking, your hero will stop moving and channel in place.

counters.text: When Clockwerk walks over his Power Cogs, they briefly retract into the ground. When retracted, they won't shock enemies if you walk into them.
Power Cogs can only shock you if you're outside the circle and you get hit by one or walk into one.
Rattletrap: Professional Salve Assassin. Try to keep Healing Salve/Clarity usage on the down low. That dude will Flare you at the worst possible times.
Rocket Flare is a popular spell to get long range kills. If you're low on HP and Clock is far away, pause for a moment once you're in fog to try to evade a potential Flare.
Hookshots are fairly easy to juke if you know they're coming. If you're trying to escape and you just walked into a Flare, stand still for a moment or change your current pathing trajectory.
Pay attention to the Flare particles. If you're in the Rosh pit and you think you're safe because you haven't gotten hit, Clock may have Flared the area a few seconds earlier.
Nature's Prophet casting Sprout on a target in Cogs will always shove everyone except the main target out of the Cogs.
Clock's Agh's Shard Jetpack ability can be dispelled.

tips.text: Rubick's Curiosity innate debuff amplification is basically the opposite of status resistance in terms of mechanics.
It could be worth carrying Blood Grenades later in the game for an easy source of damage on enemy heroes to gain Curiosity innate stacks.

Telekinesis is a damn good disable mainly because Rubick has essentially non-existent cast times. For the most part, Telekinesis can be pulled off just as quickly as a hex. So if you're worried an initiator is about to Blink in and start a team fight, keep spam casting and canceling it on their initiator so that once they Blink in range, you'll instantly pick them up.

Telekinesis being instant allows you to steal spells that good players will usually avoid letting you get. If an Earthshaker just threw out a casual Fissure, they'll almost always cover it with Enchant Totem. However, if you pluck them out of the air with an instant Telekinesis disable, you can steal their spell before they get the chance to cast another.
You can continue changing the Telekinesis Land location until the spell goes off.
notes: However, Agh's Shard Telekinesis when targeted on allies will make them land as soon as you target Telekinesis Land rather than waiting the full duration.

tips.text: If a Telekinesed enemy gets affected by any items/spells that apply forced movement or knockback, they'll immediately drop straight down and stun the area underneath.
notes: When a Telekinesed unit dies, it also immediately drops down and stuns the AoE. You can pick up a weak creep and Fade Bolt it to death to instantly get an AoE Telekinsis stun.

tips.text: If you're getting chased by multiple heroes, it can be smart to cast the Land towards you, rather than away from you. During the Lift's duration, the other enemies will have probably passed your target up, so the Land should stun them on the way back.
Agh's Shard Telekinesis allows you to throw allies out of things like an enemy Disruptor's Kinetic Field or Slark's Pounce leash.
notes: You cannot Telekinesis allies out of Enigma's Black Hole, Faceless Void's Chronosphere, or Legion Commander's Duel, so don't even bother. It'll put the spell on cooldown and do nothing if you try.

tips.text: If things are getting chaotic in a fight, know that you can target spells on allies, like Agh's Shard Telekinsis, by clicking on the allied hero's portrait in the top bar.

One of the hallmarks of a strong anti-pusher is the ability to draw aggro from a creep wave off of a tower during pushes. Fade Bolt is probably one of the strongest spells in the game to do this, mainly because of its zero cast time, huge range, damage reduction ability, and substantial nuke damage. When you want to slow down the enemy's push, cast it on the creep wave and the creeps will lose interest in hammering your tower and come for you instead.
Fade Bolt bounces always take the shortest possible distance when jumping from target to target.
Fade Bolt will not bounce to enemies that aren't in vision. If you're Fade Bolting a creep wave at night time you'll only zap the creeps you see.
Fade Bolt loses damage with each bounce, so you should generally target the ranged creep first when trying to clear waves so you can actually get the last hit with full damage.
Arcane Supremacy cast range bonuses also apply to Rubick's items.
notes: This is also true for Curiosity innate bonuses.

tips.text: You can Spell Steal through debuff immunity. Just because Enigma is a big golden teardrop doesn't mean you can't steal Black Hole through BKB.
Patience is a virtue. Don't steal spells all willy nilly. Go into a team fight knowing the spells that you would want to steal and wait for them to be cast.
Different spells are useful at different stages of the game. Sure, most ultimates are almost always worth keeping, but other spells that help Rubick farm or scout can prove valuable during downtime.

Rubick has minimal cast times on any stolen spells. Forget everything you know about landing Leshrac's Split Earth, be amazed at how you can bust out an Earthshaker Fissure in a split second, and revel in how much better a spell Zeus's Lightning Bolt is when you don't have to fist pump for half a second to cast it.

Buffs/spells/summons lingering after a Spell Steal times out or if you Steal another Spell all follow different rules. You'll just have to play a bunch of Rubick to find out what works and what doesn't.
notes: Morph's Attribute Shift is a rare example of a spell that lasts not only after Spell Steal times out, but after death. Even after many deaths.

tips.text: Stolen spell cooldowns are persistent on Rubick. If a Spell Steal is about to time out and you're sad you never got to use your stolen Tidehunter Ravage, don't just cast it for giggles. You may end up screwing yourself over in a future team fight if you steal it again.

There is a slight delay as a stolen spell "projectile" travels to your hero. You can use this window to get one last cast of your previously stolen spell, like an invisibility spell, before the new one arrives.

You can globally check if an enemy hero is an illusion or not by attempting to cast Spell Steal on them. If you clicked on an illusion, you'll immediately get an error even if you're not in cast range.
Any stolen spells that have Agh's Scepter upgrades will automatically be upgraded if you have an Agh's Scepter.
Any stolen spells that have Agh's Shard upgrades will automatically be upgraded if you have an Agh's Shard.
While Agh's Scepter allows you steal two spells, if you steal a spell that takes two slots (like Puck's Illusory Orb + Ethereal Jaunt), you'll still lose your previously stolen spell.
You can't Spell Steal Morphling's Morph or Tinker's Rearm. Balance reasons? Or because it would simply cause too many programming headaches?
notes: However, you can Spell Steal from a Morphling who is in a Morph. You could theoretically duplicate one of your teammates spells this way.

tips.text: You can Spell Steal Faceless Void's Chronosphere but Void has a unique mechanic that allows him to move in any Chronosphere regardless of who cast it.

Spells that repeatedly drain mana, like Leshrac's Pulse Nova or Storm Sprit's Ball Lightning, do not have their draining mana cost reduced. Only the initial cost is reduced by Spell Steal. Mana cost reduction mechanics do not work on any abilities that drain mana over time on any hero.
You can use Earth Spirit's own Stone Remnants with your stolen versions of his spells.
With Agh's Shard, you can cast a stolen Life Drain into an enemy Pugna's Nether Ward.

counters.text: Rubick being in your lane automatically adds an extra danger range that you need to keep in your safety zone because of Telekinesis's repositioning ability. Don't let him into your zone.
Remember that Rubick has much better cast range on your abilities than you do thanks to Arcane Supremacy.

Rubick is all about capitalizing on your forgetfulness/laziness. "Oh right, they have a Rubick, I'm Tidehunter and I should have cast Anchor Smash after Ravage. I'm Mars and I should have cast Bulwark after Arena. I'm Batrider and I should have cast Sticky Napalm after Flaming Lasso." Put a condom on all of your spells, it's 99% effective.
Always check what spell Rubick has stolen by clicking on him. If you're Pudge and Rubick just Ghostbuster'd your essence, face your shame and tell your team that he has stolen Meat Hook, not Rot.

tips.text: Your Fowl Play innate will not protect you from a lethal Axe Culling Blade or Necrophos Reaper's Scythe.
notes: It will protect you from a lethal amount of damage after Oracle's False Promise ends, though.

tips.text: Ether Shock can hit secondary units almost twice as far away than the spell's cast range. If an enemy is making a run for it and is just out of cast range, try casting the Shock on the ranged creep right behind them to possibly hit them. Ether Shock won't bounce to units that are in fog, however.
Ether Shock chooses secondary targets in a cone in front of Shadow Shaman. Secondary targets are always the closest available units to the primary target.

The facts on Hex: Instant cast time, insta-kills illusions (except 'strong' illusions like Venge's Agh's Scepter Vengeance illusion), and is super annoying. Spam cast and cancel this spell on the enemy team's initiator when you're toeing off. The moment they Blink in and are in range, they'll be Rhasta Fried Chicken.
notes: Hexes are effectively casting a silence, a mute, and a slow on enemies. Some enemies can cast spells while stunned (like Abaddon with Borrowed Time), but can't during a hex because they're silenced.

tips.text: An enemy will always be able to activate BKB in-between Shackle and Hex. Lead with Hex during ganks, especially since Hex has no cast animation and also has longer range.
Shackles provides true sight on the target.
You can cast Agh's Scepter Shackles on any couriers on your team and use them as Ether Shocking drones. Just be aware of the break distance.
You can trap enemies inside your Wards by targeting the circle directly onto a hero. Unless they have something like Phase Boots, they'll be trapped by the collision of all the Wards.
Serpent Wards are controllable units. Be sure to keep Wards focused on your most important target, like the enemy tower, before they got distracted in a team fight.
Serpent Wards can attack other types of ward units, like Pugna's Nether Ward or Undying's Tombstone.

Don't let enemies farm your Serpent Wards for free after they win a team fight. It only takes a few attacks from a hero to kill a Ward. Select one lone Ward in the back and have it murder its siblings with a deny when they're down to 1 HP.
Serpent Wards have 1200/800 day/night vision.
Serpent Wards can benefit from the attack speed buff provided by Chen's Penitence.
Serpent Wards are frozen inside Faceless Void's Chronosphere. Place the Wards outside of the Chrono if you want to hit enemies inside.
Tier 1 towers never have backdoor protection enabled, only Tier 2 onwards have it. Keep this in mind if you want to sneak a quick Tier 1 tower with Serpent Wards without a creep wave.

Sentry wards can tank ten hits from a tower before they die. If you're trying to sneakily take a tower and you really want to make sure it goes down, consider plopping down a sentry ward to draw the tower's aggro and then casting Serpent Wards. I guess you could also burn an observer ward for this strat, but you better have a huge lead if you're doing that.

counters.text: If you're trapped in a circle of Serpent Wards, you can Phase through the Serpents using Phase Boots or certain invis abilities.
Damage block does not mitigate Serpent Ward damage. All ward-type units ignore damage block, like from Vanguard.
Casting Serpent Wards costs a ton of mana, making Shaman a great candidate for mana burning or Pugna Nether Warding against.
Illusion attacks count as hero attacks against Serpent Wards.
You can break these cuffs. Always have a stun/silence ready on your team to bail a teammate out from the Shackle channel.
notes: Banishes can also free allies from channeled disables, like Shackles.

counters.text: Lotus Orb can help discourage Shadow Shaman from chain disabling allies.

Keep a Blood Grenade handy in lane to finish off a Shadow Shaman who may otherwise narrowly escape with his Fowl Play innate. Just be sure to cast it after the innate procs because it also dispels him on trigger.
Breaks can disable Shadow Shaman's Fowl Play innate.
notes: Breaks can be provided with items like Silver Edge or Khanda. Spells that Break include Doom's Agh's Scepter Doom, Hoodwink's Sharpshooter, Naga Siren's Agh's Scepter Ensnare, Nyx Assassin's Vendetta, Phantom Assassin's Agh's Scepter Fan of Knives, Shadow Demon's Agh's Scepter Demonic Purge, Viper's Viper Strike, and a few others.

counters.text: A lethal Axe Culling Blade or Necrophos Reaper's Scythe can kill Shadow Shaman through his Fowl Play innate.

tips.text: You can cast Guardian Sprint while TPing and it won't cancel the channel.
Guardian Sprint gives Slardar 100% slow resistance for the first few seconds of the buff.
Slithereen Crush's puddle and the water trail from Corrosive Haze buffs your Seaborn Sentinel innate the same way being in the river would.
notes: Make a puddle with Crush when pushing towers to benefit from the bonus passive damage from Seaborn Sentinel.

tips.text: Slithereen Crush and Bash procs deal physical damage, making them work very well with Corrosive Haze's armor reduction.
Increase your Bash attack counter on jungle or lane creeps. The buff lasts indefinitely and won't increase/proc on building or ward targets.
Basher/Abyssal passive bashes don't work with Slardar. The game won't allow you to have another bash besides Bash of the Deep.
Bash of the Deep can stun enemies through spell immunity/BKB.
Corrosive Haze's armor reduction makes taking Rosh or Tormentor much easier for your team.
Corrosive Haze's true sight isn't some sort of get-out-of-buying-detection-free card. The way to counter invis heroes is to know where they are before they know you know where they are.
Corrosive Haze fully works on debuff immune/BKB'd enemies.
You can cast Corrosive Haze on enemy couriers.

counters.text: Slardar's Guardian Sprint can be dispelled.
Guardian Sprint gives Slardar 100% slow resistance for the first few seconds of the buff.
Be aware that Corrosive Haze's armor reduction can allow the enemy team to take Roshan super early.
Corrosive Haze provides true sight on any debuffed targets.
Corrosive Haze can be removed with basic dispels like from Lotus Orb, Guardian Greaves, Manta Style, Disperser, or Satanic.
notes: Slardar has a "Corrosive Haze Undispellable" talent.

tips.text: Capitalize on Essence Shift innate stacks. Take a tower or TP to another lane and use all the damage you have to continue snowballing. Don't just sit around and farm, the enemy should be scared of how much damage you have after winning a fight.
You will lose all Essence Shift innate stacks on death, including deaths from Aegis. The enemies will still be missing their stats for the full duration, however.
You need to be within 300 range of a target dying with the Essence Shift innate debuff to get the permanent AGI. Or if you get the kill credit, the enemy can be at any range.
Each tick of Dark Pact strong dispels Slark. In addition to most standard debuffs, strong dispels can even remove stuns.

Dark Pact can't remove a lot of things despite being a strong dispel. A few undispellable debuffs worth keeping in mind are: Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast, Bloodseeker's Rupture, Invoker's Deafening Blast, Witch Doctor's Maledict, Razor's Static Link, Ursa's Fury Swipes, or Viper's Viper Strike. If you want to get rid of these spells, too bad.

Dark Pact is a 'nuke' like Lifestealer's Infest can be a 'nuke.' Yes, the spell can deal healthy damage, but that's not its only purpose. Don't yank the Pact ripcord the second you get in melee range of your gank target. Wait for them to turn around, or for their teammate to come in to save them, then pull the trigger and wipe off any potential disable. If you need to use Dark Pact for damage, only use it if you're sure the enemy can't disable you or try to save it for the killing blow.
Pounce won't latch illusions, making it useful for identifying the real Chaos Knight/Phantom Lancer/Naga Siren.
Pounce can hit and leash invisible units, but it won't give any vision of them.
Pounce connects with debuff immune/BKB'd targets and you will get Essence Shift innate stacks, but the leash won't restrict their movement.
Leashing enemies with Pounce can cancel TPs and prevent them from casting most movement spells while leashed. Mechanically, leashes function very similarly to roots.
Take advantage of your free pathing state in Pounce when you're escaping. Don't just leap along down the lane, jump over a tree line or clear a cliff to create a gap.

Orienting Pounces to go where you want them to can sometimes be challenging when the game's pathing doesn't cooperate. A handy way to work around this is by enabling the "Holding ALT Enables Directional Move" option in settings. This command makes it so that whenever you're holding down ALT, your hero ignores pathing and tries to move in a straight line towards where you right clicked.
notes: You can also enable the "Directional Move" hotkey in the settings, but this ALT modifier may be easier to use once you get used to it.
Directional move can also be helpful for aiming spells when escaping over cliffs like Mirana's Leap, Pangolier's Shield Crash, Ursa's Earthshock, or Zeus's Heavenly Jump.

tips.text: The passive from Shadow Dance can be very useful for counterwarding. If you're walking around and you lose the Shadow Dance regen buff, you'll know you've wandered into enemy vision.
notes: So carry your own sentry wards. I'm serious. Yes, I know you're a carry, you've probably never clicked on the item in your life, but do it. Did you know observer wards give gold when you kill them? It's a net profit, I promise.

tips.text: Enemies can still see the TP particle effect when you start channeling under Shadow Dance.
Slark is one of few heroes that has 1800 night vision.
You can't cast Shadow Dance while channeling a TP unlike other invis spells, but you can activate Shadow Blade/Silver Edge mid-channel.

counters.text: Slark's Essence Shift innate is the long con. You may think you're winning these exchanges in lane because Slark has awful HP, but he's gaining a Slipper of Agility and you're losing an Iron Branch's worth of stats every time you trade hits.
You'll get your Essence Shifted stats back when you respawn, but Slark will still have them as well. This is true for Aegis respawns as well.

Dark Pact strong dispels as often as it damages, meaning that there are 10 little mini-dispels throughout the duration of the spell. So don't bother trying to stun Slark mid-Pact, just wait for the spell to end.

If Slark Pounces on you, don't just immediately mash your stuns on him. Bad Slarks usually pop Dark Pact the moment they jump on someone because most enemies panic and use their disables as soon as this fishy boy starts stabbing them. Instead, accept the fact that you got caught, gamble that a Dark Pact is about to come out, then use your stun after you see Pact used.
notes: If you're playing against a smart Slark, you can go one layer deeper and cast and cancel your stun spell animation to bait out the Dark Pact.
Keep an eye on his mana bar to verify if he actually cast Dark Pact or not.

counters.text: Ground targeted spells (especially ground targeted stuns like Lina's Light Strike Array, Leshrac's Split Earth, Nyx's Impale, etc) are highly valuable against Slark for hassling him whenever he activates Shadow Dance.

Inexperienced Slarks have a tendency of going for long-range Pounces which are fairly easy to juke. Line yourself up with him when you're getting chased to tease the Pounce out, then move straight left or right and dodge it.

If you manage to move your hero outside the edge of the Pounce leash, it'll break. That means weird things that provide collision, like planting an Iron Branch or getting shoved by Earthshaker Fissure or Tusk Ice Shards will break the leash. So do other repositioning spells, like getting kicked by an Earth Spirit Boulder Smash, getting Meat Hooked by Pudge, or even a lucky Manta Style rearrangement.
notes: If you go for the Manta Style method, your best bet is to activate Phase Boots before Mirror Image to reduce your chances of collision with an illusion pushing you back into the leash.

If you go for the Branch planting method, either portrait casting or casting the Branch inside your hero's selection circle between your hero model and the leash is surprisingly reliable at breaking out of a Pounce. This Branch trick also works against Disruptor's Kinetic Field.

counters.text: You can't Force Staff out of Slark's Pounce leash, but you can break the leash by Hurricane Piking any target that isn't yourself.
notes: Piking any target that isn't yourself works. You can even Pike an ally, which is theoretically just like using a Force Staff on them, and it'll free you from Pounce leash.
However, if an ally is Pounce leashed, you can't use Pike on them to save them.

counters.text: Debuff immunity/BKB allows you to walk out of Slark's Pounce leash.
If Slark is trying to escape, attempt to intercept his Pounce out by standing in front of him so he'll hit your hero instead of making a getaway over a cliff.
Slark cannot Pounce when rooted/leashed.
Slark's Essence Shift innate gaining new stacks and HP regen from the Shadow Dance passive can both be disabled by breaks.
notes: Breaks can be provided with items like Silver Edge or Khanda. Spells that Break include Doom's Agh's Scepter Doom, Hoodwink's Sharpshooter, Naga Siren's Agh's Scepter Ensnare, Nyx Assassin's Vendetta, Phantom Assassin's Agh's Scepter Fan of Knives, Shadow Demon's Agh's Scepter Demonic Purge, Viper's Viper Strike, and a few others.
Silver Edge and Khanda's Breaks are especially strong against Slark since they cannot be dispelled.

counters.text: Ghost Scepter can help supports survive Slark ganks.
Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast can prevent Slark from healing even during his active Shadow Dance and can't be dispelled.

Bloodseeker notably counters the dickens out of Slark. Slark doesn't like to be silenced, he can't Dark Pact off Rupture, and if he loses too much HP he'll make BS Thirsty and give him global true sight, thus preventing his Shadow Dance passive regen.
Spirit Breaker is irritating for Slark to deal with since Dark Pact can't dispel Charge and since Charge will provide vision the whole time, Slark can't regen with his Shadow Dance passive.
Slark can't dispel Disruptor's Glimpse, making the full combo of Static Storm+Kinetic Field often lethal.
Naga Siren's Song turns off Slark's Shadow Dance active and reveals him, thus stopping Slark from regening and being invisible. The Dance will continue once the Song ends, though.
Gleipnir can root Slark even when he's untargetable in Shadow Dance.

Dust has a weird interaction with Dark Pact + Shadow Dance. Dust applies damage to any targets that are "invisible." While Shadow Dance isn't traditional invisibility that gets revealed by Dust, Dust still damages a Slark in Shadow Dance anyway. The funny part is if Slark activates Dark Pact while under Shadow Dance in Dust's AoE, he'll get damaged for every single time Dust gets purged off and then instantly reapplied.
notes: Dust damaging weird types of invisibility also applies to Dusting enemies who are Smoked. Could be a clever way to break Blink Daggers if you're being ganked.

tips.text: When farming neutral camps, kill the smaller creeps first. That way you can proc your Desolate innate damage on the big creep.
Spectral Dagger gives shared vision on every enemy that get hits by the projectile. This allows you to get basic vision (not true sight, just location) on invis enemies.

If your hero is within ~1800 range of a neutral camp, you can draw aggro and stack it if you damage the camp, like with Spectral Dagger. Any further away and neutrals won't aggro your hero when damaged and just keep sitting in their camp.
Spectral Dagger ignores Lotus Orbs.
Spectral Dagger can bypass Linken's Sphere if ground targeted.

Spectre gets a 1 second grace period of free pathing after walking off a Spectral Dagger trail. So if you're trying to escape and don't need to create a huge gap, you can toss the Dagger at your enemies to slow them and then escape backwards over a cliff or across some trees.
Spectre illusions can also benefit from the Spectral Dagger trail's free pathing.
You can't use Spectral Dagger's free pathing to get out of spells like Disruptor's Kinetic Field or Mars's Arena, but you can Reality to an illusion that's outside to escape.

Shadow Step illusions have a long enough duration to allow you to toss one out, TP back to base, get some regen or grab items from your stash, then Reality back to the illusion (assuming they didn't kill it).
Dispersion reflects damage before any reductions are calculated. This means it will deal damage before calculating any armor/magic resistance/barriers.
Spectre doesn't have a farming steroid like most carries. However, Haunt allows her to perpetually farm lanes or split push since she can instantly participate in a team fight on demand.

You're invulnerable when flying to an illusion when casting Reality. You can use this to run head first into projectiles like Gyrocopter's Homing Missile to negate the stun/damage. If your timing is godlike, you can even use the travel invulnerability to dodge things like the AoE stun from Phoenix's Supernova.
You can use Reality multiple times during a Haunt cast.
If a target dies, the corresponding Haunt illusion will vanish as well.
Casting Haunt can be a handy way to break enemy initiator Blink Daggers even if you don't have vision of them.

counters.text: Spectral Dagger creates a trail on invis units if you took damage from the spell.
Shadow Step and Haunt illusions have free pathing and will follow you over cliffs. These illusions can be slowed and stunned.
Any level of Dagon can instakill illusions. As do spells like Disruptor's Glimpse, Pudge's Meat Hook, Skywrath Mage's Mystic Flare, and any Hex.
notes: Brewmaster's Storm Brewling with Dispel Magic deals full damage to all types of illusions.

counters.text: Enchantress can take control of enemy illusions with Enchant.

Whenever Spectre Shadow Steps, stand next to your creeps or give your teammates a hug. For most of the early to mid game her only illusion damage is coming from her Desolate innate, so don't let it proc.
Spectre's Desolate innate and Dispersion passives can be disabled by breaks.
notes: Breaks can be provided with items like Silver Edge or Khanda. Spells that Break include Doom's Agh's Scepter Doom, Hoodwink's Sharpshooter, Naga Siren's Agh's Scepter Ensnare, Nyx Assassin's Vendetta, Phantom Assassin's Agh's Scepter Fan of Knives, Shadow Demon's Agh's Scepter Demonic Purge, Viper's Viper Strike, and a few others.

counters.text: Mage Slayer reduces all spell damage from enemies, potentially making it useful at mitigating Dispersion or Desolate innate damage from Spectre.
Spectres generally don't like building BKB or MKB, so magic damage and evasion may prove to be more useful against her compared to other carries.
Spectre cannot travel to illusions with Reality if she's rooted.

tips.text: Static Remnants last quite a while, so it's not a bad idea to set some up if you're afraid a Riki or Smoked hero is trailing you since they'll detonate and damage on invis units.
You can drop a Static Remnant on an Aegis reincarnation to prevent the enemy from Blinking out since the Remnant will detonate as soon as the enemy respawns.
Toggling the alt-cast on Static Remnant will cause the spell to cast directly on Storm Spirit.

You can Overload an auto attack while the projectile is flying in the air. If you just tossed a long range auto attack on a target, you can cast a Remnant or Ball real quick and the attack will hit Overloaded.

Get your free Overloads. Cast a spell in the fountain or throw up a quick Remnant once you reach your destination if you're going to be TPing to a tower. Or use a spell before activating an invis rune.
You can cast spells like Static Remnant or Electric Vortex while flying in Ball Lightning.
You can use items while in Ball Lightning, like Scythe of Vyse or Orchid.
notes: You can begin channeling a TP while flying in Ball Lightning. Useful when escaping or during base defenses to kill a creep wave while zipping and TPing back to safety at the same time.
You can pick up items while flying in Ball Lightning. Like an Aegis, perhaps.
You can pick up runes that are along your path while in Ball Lightning. You can activate runes and use Bottle while in Ball.

tips.text: You can start a drive-by Outpost or Watcher channel by clicking them during Ball Lightning.
notes: Channeling a Twin Gate will immediately cancel Ball Lightning movement.

tips.text: While traveling in Ball Lightning, Storm will attempt to perform the next action you ordered once he gets in range to do it. If there is no action (like a right click on the enemy hero), he'll just auto attack the nearest thing if Auto Attack is set to 'Standard.'
notes: This can be irritating when you're Balling long distances or into fogged vision because Storm may waste the Overload attack on a creep that's in attack range while mid-Ball. To avoid this, hit the 'Cancel Current Action'/stop key while you're flying and he won't attack anything while flying and he'll do nothing when he lands.
If you lose your Overload attack while flying in Ball Lightning, you can just re-cast Ball Lightning mid-flight and you'll get another Overload charge for free.

tips.text: If you need escape quickly when an enemy is setting up on you, be cognizant of your turn rate. You may be better off doing a quick zip forward rather than risking turning around in front of the enemy.

Avoid making multiple short trips when you're escaping and Balling on a mana budget. Do one long trip. There's no reason to have to pay the ignition cost of Ball Lightning multiple times if you have one destination.
Ball Lightning disjoints projectiles on cast.
You can cast a 0 range Ball Lightning by clicking your hero portrait when targeting Ball.
notes: If you have the "Double Tap Ability to Self Cast" setting enabled, you can also double tap Ball Lightning to cast it in place to get an Overload or for the disjoint.

tips.text: If you Ball Lightning over the edges of the map, you briefly get high ground vision over the surrounding treeline.

If you Ball Lightning over the edges of the map at an angle, you'll be placed back onto the map without breaking any trees behind you. If you're trying to escape enemies chasing you in the trees, consider doing this instead of zipping down every tree in a straight line.

You are considered 'invulnerable' while in Ball Lightning (similar to being in a Eul's cyclone), so brush up on your jukenomics. Besides using the invulnerability to absorb projectiles (like flying into a Wraith King's Wraithfire Blast), ticks from damage over time sources like Queen of Pain's Shadow Strike, delayed stuns like Dark Willow's Cursed Crown, or even damage from Bloodseeker's Rupture, can all be dodged while in Ball Lightning.
notes: Invulnerability also means most debuffs can't be applied to you while you're in Ball Lightning. This allows you to do things like attack an Enchantress mid-Ball Lightning and bypass Untouchable applying the attack speed debuff.
You can also do things like fly through a Faceless Void's Chronosphere in Ball Lightning.

You are not considered 'hidden/banished' in Ball Lightning. That means certain spells that affect invulnerable units, like Silencer's Global Silence and Disruptor's Static Storm, can still debuff you while you're in Ball Lightning.

Since you are invulnerable while in Ball Lightning, you can cast items like Orchid on a target with Lotus Orb and not worry about it getting reflected back. You can also avoid a reflected Electric Vortex, but you have to target Ball Lightning far enough away that the 0.3s cast animation of Vortex takes place while you're still in Ball Lightning.

tips.text: If you need to chain multiple Ball Lightning casts as quickly as possible, you need to try and time your next Ball Lightning when you're slightly less than 0.3s away from the first Ball Lightning ending. This way most of the cast animation for the next zip happens as the previous zip is ending. If you do it too early, Storm Spirit won't do anything when the first Ball Lightning ends. If you do it too late, you'll be vulnerable for a brief moment during the new zip's cast animation. This is mainly relevant during high ground defenses where you need to shoot out of your base to kill the creep wave and return back as safely as possible.
Doing multiple quick Ball Lightnings is a great way to torture heroes who have long cast animations. They'll have to keep turning and resetting their cast animation every time you Ball around them.

Arcane Rune (and other sources of mana cost reduction) only reduce Ball Lightning's initial mana cost, not the travel cost. Mana cost reduction mechanics do not work on any abilities that drain mana over time on any hero.
Remember that Regen Runes end once your hero is at max HP/mana. Keep zipping around and farming with Ball Lightning to keep yourself below max mana to take advantage of the full rune duration.

counters.text: Shut his mouth. Silences and most other disables irritate Storm. The more time he has to spend walking around with non-Overloaded right clicks, the less happy he is.

Break his ankles. Like most other heroes with a Blink, Storms will overshoot Ball Lightning down the path that they think you're traveling so they can get in more right clicks. If you're escaping out of his auto attack range during a gank, as soon as he starts Balling towards you, turn around and move to where he just was. He'll either have to Ball again or slowly walk to come back.
Tie him up. Storm can't cast Ball Lightning when rooted. Heroes with roots/leashes are obviously great, but don't forget about Rod of Atos.
Ghost Scepter is an underrated item against Storm. Yes, most of his damage is magic, but he actually has to right click on you to deal it.
Mana burn can be annoying for Storm to deal with. Anti-Mage, for example, loves going up against Storm Spirits.
Nyx Assassin can be annoying for Storm to deal with since he may inadvertently trigger Spiked Carapace with Overload or Static Remnant's AoEs.

Disruptor's Agh's Scepter Static Storm can mute invulnerable targets. If a Storm Spirit keeps killing your creep wave with repeated Ball Lightning+TP combos when you're trying to siege his high ground, you can risk catching him by surprise by canceling his TP with an early Static Storm in his Ball Lightning path. As he flies through it, he'll get muted and his TP will get canceled.

If you're Roshing and you suspect Storm may attempt to snatch the Aegis, try dropping some useless items like your Quelling Blade or Wraith Bands around Rosh. While he's frantically trying to pick up an Aegis, he may end up jamming his inventory with your decoy items.
Before Storm hits level 6, he's pretty vulnerable to ganks with his slow move speed and no escapes. Consider rotating to gank him early on in the game to slow him down.
The Overload buff can be dispelled off Storm Spirit.
notes: Agh's Shard Overload can be dispelled off enemies.

tips.text: Storm Hammer stuns and damages everything in its AoE. If an enemy has Linken's Sphere, but is sitting inside their creep wave, just target the Hammer on a creep.
Warcry works fully on illusions and creep-heroes (Brewmaster's Primal Split Brewlings, Visage's Familiars, or Warlock's Golem).

God's Strength multiplies Sven's primary attribute/base damage. Meaning, when you go full WOLOLO, only damage from STR is getting multiplied, but items that are adding green + damage (raw damage items) aren't get multiplied.
Agh's Scepter Storm Hammer can dispel things like Ghost Scepter or spells like Windranger's Windrun off enemies.
notes: The dispel affects everything in the AoE, meaning you can even dispel Ringmaster's Escape Act or a Eul's cyclone if they're in the AoE.

tips.text: Unlike most mobility spells, Agh's Scepter Storm Hammer is not disabled by roots/leashes. You can even travel in and out of Mars's Arena thanks to the invulnerability as well.

counters.text: Storm Hammer's projectile can be disjointed.
Warcry can be removed off Sven and his allies with basic dispels.
notes: Agh's Shard Warcry cannot be dispelled.

counters.text: Cleave damage, like from Great Cleave, can be reduced by armor.
Breaks can disable Sven's Wrath of God innate and Great Cleave.
At a certain point in the game, Sven chunks so hard that you won't even be able to react and survive his initiation. An Aeon Disk could save your life in these situations.
